checks.issue: Confirmed in the DK 2019 OCR, lines 27252-27254: 'Their skin and bones are three times as dense as those of a human and they are almost invulnerable to physical attack. They possess great strength (most are able to lift 30 tons) and, due to their density, weigh far more than humans of comparable size.' The Enchantress caption reads 'Asgardian body three times denser and heavier than that of a normal human being.' Thor's factfile reads 'HEIGHT 6ft6 in WEIGHT 640 Ibs' (OCR) and '...vast magical abilities provided by the Odinforce', with no density statement. Marvel.com Thor reads 'Thor: 640 lbs., Donald Blake: 150 lbs.' with no density statement. Not re-verified: the DK 2014 snippet. Its full-text query returned HTTP 502 three times.

I recomputed every number. 640 lb = 290.3 kg, and /3 = 96.77 kg (213.3 lb). The S values are 67.19/60.47/57.12 (listed) and 22.40/20.16/19.04 (adjusted). Plain FFMI is 24.65/22.19. Blake scaled isometrically comes out at 216.7 lb. All match. Two problems with how it is presented. (1) The 'about plus or minus a third' uncertainty is not carried into the S values. With a factor of 2-4, or 97 kg plus or minus a third, S at 10% fat runs from about 13-15 to about 27-30, not '20-22'. (2) S of 20-22 is below the brief's US Army median (about 24). The number is the handbook's round-number arithmetic, not a description of the heavily muscled figure Marvel draws. It must not be presented as Thor's muscle level.
checks.corrected: Show S_equiv as a range: about 15-30 at 10% fat for a density factor of 2-4. Label it 'what the handbook's density figure implies, derived', not 'Thor's build'.

The official quotes are confirmed. Marvel.com: 'Most of Fisk's bulk is actually muscle, not fat; his enormous size is comparable to that of a sumo wrestler', 'HEIGHT 6'7"' and 'WEIGHT 450 lbs.' OHOTMU vol 1: 'His great bulk does not consist of fat but of muscles that have been developed to enormous size, as' and 'as in a sumo wrestler. The Kingpin can lift (press) approximately 650 pounds.' Recomputed: FFM 200.03, FFMI 49.68, S 44.57, S at 15% fat 38.65, 9/450 = 2.0%. These match. The error: the notes say the fan-wiki '9 pounds' sentence 'carries no citation'. It does. The re-fetched wikitext ends that bullet with {{r|Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe: Daredevil 2004 Vol 1 1}}. The figure is attributed to an official handbook, which has not been verified, so it is not simply 'fan-wiki only'. Missing caveat: the official analogy is a sumo wrestler, and sumo wrestlers are not lean. So 'does not consist of fat' should not be read as near-zero fat.

checks.issue: Several classes go beyond the evidence or are applied inconsistently. (a) Thing 'overstated': official text only calls the skin rock-like and 'supple'. The density claim is fan-wiki. Without that, the direction is unknown. (b) Superman 'comparable': DK 2021 says Kryptonians have a 'dense molecular structure'. Under the researcher's own rule for Luke Cage, that makes him 'overstated, amount unknown'. (c) Hulk, Abomination and Doc Samson have a 'fortified cellular structure', which is treated as comparable, while Cage's 'dense' tissue is treated as overstated. Defensible, since only Cage's sources say 'dense', but say so. (d) Thor plot_mass_kg 96.8 is given as a point when the factor is only 'about three', and Thor himself has Asgardian attributes 'to a much greater degree' (2004 handbook). 1. The DK DC 2021 Kryptonians entry ('dense molecular structure', no factor) is missing. Superman needs it, and the comic tooltips should quote it.
2. The researcher said the 2004-2010 handbooks could not be searched. They can: OHOTMU Avengers part one 2004 (officialhandbook0000unse_z5q7), OHOTMU 2008 (officialhandbook0000unse_i8k4) and OHOTMU Spider-Man 2006 (marvelencycloped00jona) are all full-text searchable on archive.org. Search them for:
   - the Thor, Captain America, Luke Cage, Black Panther and Kingpin entries;
   - Thor's own density wording. The 2004 entry says 'attributes of an Asgardian god, but to a much greater degree', and Hercules there is 'several times denser'.
3. Kingpin's 9 lb of fat is still unverified in OHOTMU: Daredevil 2004, the issue the fan wiki cites. Try the 2006 Spider-Man handbook; it can be reached, although my 'sumo' and 'fat' queries returned HTTP 502.
4. The Hulk's height and weight line in the Deluxe handbook, so that 'over 800 pounds' is tied to that edition's own figures.
5. The OHOTMU Deluxe entries for the Thing, Wolverine and Thor. They are not in Essential vol 1, and I found no later Essential volumes on archive.org.
6. The DK 2014 Asgardian snippet and the 'steel-hard skin' clean snippet could not be re-verified. Both queries returned HTTP 502 on every try.
7. Citations: every archive.org full-text search URL should come with the item's details URL, because that API often returns 502 (about half of the cited queries failed on first fetch on 2026-10-11).
8. The density-factor uncertainty for Thor (about 2-4) is not propagated into the recommended S range.
9. The brief assumes some of the Thing's weight is rock. The research found no official basis for that, so the page should not state it as fact.
verdict:
The quotes and numbers hold up; the problems are in how some claims are labelled. I re-fetched more than 40 sources: 12 Marvel.com pages, three DK OCR texts, about 25 archive.org full-text queries, 11 fan-wiki pages and archive.org metadata. Every Marvel.com and DK quotation I could reach matches. Every derived S and FFMI value recomputes correctly, with Kingpin's S at 15% fat 38.65, so 38.6 or 38.7. The handbook wording for Asgardians, Colossus, the Hulk, Abomination, Kingpin and Juggernaut is confirmed, including Juggernaut's 900 lb line.

Six things need correcting:
1. The DC finding is wrong. DK's DC Comics Encyclopedia (2021) gives Kryptonians a 'dense molecular structure', so Superman has an official, unquantified density statement. It is not fan-wiki only.
2. The fan wiki's Kingpin '9 pounds of fat' does have a citation, to OHOTMU: Daredevil 2004. It is reported and unverified, not 'fan-wiki only' and not uncited.
3. The Angel 'devoid of fat' quote was taken from the unauthorised kileko_empire upload, not from OHOTMU Deluxe vol 1, which has different wording.
4. 'The Thing: not a body of rock' and 'Juggernaut: mystical, not material' are the researcher's inferences, not what the sources say.
5. The 'overstated' class for the Thing has no official support.
6. A 'none found' search result should not have the status official.

On the recommendations:
- Recommendation 1 overstates the evidence. It makes Thor's main point 96.8 kg, S about 20-22, which is below the US Army median. That rests on a round in-universe 'about three times' factor, and the 2004 handbook says Thor has Asgardian attributes 'to a much greater degree'. Show it as a range, about 15-30 at 10% fat, labelled as what the handbook's arithmetic implies.
- Recommendation 9 ('no Marvel or DC source gives any body-fat percentage') must become 'none found in the sources searched'. The 2004-2010 handbooks were not fully searched, and one fat figure is attributed to them.
- Recommendations 2, 3, 5, 6 and 10 are sound.
- Recommendation 4 is sound for Luke Cage but not for the Thing.
- Recommendation 7 is sound.
- Recommendation 8 is sound once the Kingpin attribution is corrected and the sumo caveat is added.
- Superman should get Luke Cage's treatment: overstated by an unknown amount.
